standard.title: Resilience and identities
standard.description: investigate how success, challenge, setbacks and failure strengthen resilience and identities in a range of contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have described their personal qualities and those of others, and explained how they contribute to developing identities (AC9HP2P01). They understand personal qualities but have not yet examined how experiences of success, setback and failure shape identity and resilience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate how success, challenge, setbacks and failure strengthen resilience and identities in a range of contexts.

nodes.label: Stories of challenge and success
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how characters or people overcome challenge and adversity and achieve success in different ways.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse at least one story or example of a person overcoming a challenge, identifying what the challenge was, how they responded, and what the outcome was for their identity or resilience.
nodes.typical_width: Examine multiple stories and examples (from texts, sport, community, peers) of overcoming challenge; identify patterns in how people respond to adversity and what builds resilience.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australians' pride in cultural background strengthens identity and resilience — exploring stories of First Nations athletes, leaders or community members.
Explore how responses to success, challenge, setbacks and failure are shaped by cultural beliefs and values — comparing examples from different cultural contexts.
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that challenge and setback contribute to rather than undermine identity is the core conceptual shift of this standard. Without it, students' work on resilience strategies (node 2) has no conceptual grounding — they treat resilience as a technique rather than an outcome of how one relates to difficulty.

response_modes.reason: Students often conflate success with positive identity development and failure with negative — the key insight that challenge and failure are also identity-strengthening requires explicit discussion and counterexample. Text-based case analysis with guided questions builds this reasoning.

First Nations Australian perspectives on resilience and identity, and cross-cultural comparisons of responses to adversity, offer substantively different frameworks for understanding how identity is built — not just additional examples. Exploring these contexts enriches the conceptual understanding meaningfully.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations and cross-cultural perspectives on resilience and identity represent a substantive and meaningful enrichment direction — not just additional examples but alternative conceptual frameworks for understanding how identity is built.
success_criteria: Identifies a challenge or setback a person faced in a story or real example.
Explains how the person's response to the challenge affected their resilience or identity.
Describes what 'resilience' means using language connected to a real example.

nodes.label: Unity through shared adversity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can discuss how overcoming challenge or adversity together can unite a group of diverse people.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least one example (real or from a text) where people worked through a challenge together and explain how this strengthened the group.
nodes.typical_width: Examine multiple examples of shared adversity building group connection across diverse communities; discuss what makes shared challenge a unifying experience.
wider: Explore a community event or initiative where diverse groups came together in response to a shared challenge (e.g. a natural disaster, community project) and analyse how the experience affected group identity.
Investigate the role of shared physical challenge (e.g. team sport, expedition, community sport programs) in building group resilience and identity.

response_modes.reason: The concept that shared adversity builds diverse communities is best explored across multiple group contexts — classroom, sport team, community, cultural group — rather than through a single case study.

success_criteria: Describes an example of people overcoming a challenge together.
Explains how shared challenge contributed to group connection or unity.
Identifies what was different about the group after experiencing the challenge together.

nodes.label: Physical activity and identity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise how success, challenge, failure and enjoyment of physical activities influence identities.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe how one experience of success, challenge or failure in a physical activity affected how they felt about themselves.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on a range of physical activity experiences (success, struggle, failure, enjoyment) and explain how each influenced their developing sense of identity and confidence.
wider: Design a journal or reflective record of physical activity experiences that tracks identity and confidence changes over a unit, identifying patterns in what builds and what challenges their sense of self.
Compare how different students in the class connect physical activity to identity — exploring why the same experience (e.g. team sport) can have very different identity effects for different people.

response_modes.reason: This node integrates the abstract understanding of challenge and resilience from node 1 with students' direct lived experience of physical activity. The teaching focus should bridge the two — helping students see their own PE experiences as identity-relevant.

success_criteria: Describes a specific physical activity experience involving success, challenge or failure.
Explains how the experience affected their confidence or sense of self.
Connects the experience to the idea of resilience or identity development.
